result:
I've planned round 233 and set the decision to **CONTINUE**. It is a short bug-fix round before SABA-B-7, because the final CALM-3 stage of SABA-B-8 passed but the gate review found a Medium bug in it.

**What round 232 left:** C passed all 18 rows in the real browser at both viewports, and the gate published `bd71144`, which is the new baseline. The only blocked row is the Mac check, which needs a Mac. The gate reviewer then found that pressing Ctrl+Alt+O while the Overview has keyboard focus drops focus to `body`. C's own measurement shows it, and I reproduced it in Chromium at the baseline. My round-232 task had specified exactly that behaviour, so this is my spec error.

**Round 233 (`current-task.md`):**
- **GATE232-S1 (Medium):** when the focused Overview is hidden, focus moves to the next Tab stop: the video expand button when docked, the placeholder's return button when the video floats. Showing the Overview moves no focus, and focus on any other control is never moved. I rejected the reviewer's suggested target, the timeline scroller, because it can't take focus. New test OV-T6 fails without the fix.
- **C-R232-01 (Low):** the render-budget "Play → Pause → Play" test took 56 % of its timeout at the gate itself. It now declares 15000 ms, like the test next to it.
- **Scope:** three changed files plus a new doc 181. The protected auth and purchase files stay frozen.
- **Pre-check:** on a scratch copy outside the repo, typecheck and lint are clean and all 32 covering test files (542 tests) pass. The scratch build behaves as specified in the browser.

**Other gate findings:**
- **AltGr on Windows (Medium):** may stop Ctrl+Alt+O working on some layouts. The cloud browser can't produce AltGr, so it goes on the Tech Lead manual list as TLM-R232-ALTGR-WIN and doesn't block, per the 2026-10-23 root rule.
- **Three Lows:** deferred to the polish list.
- **Two architecture notes:** kept as signals and added to the SABA-B-8 end checkpoint request, which root can run now.

**Backlog gap:** Saba's approved SABA-B-9/10/11 (transport, Insert Marker, musical grid) had no backlog entry. I added it after SABA-B-7 with his six stages in his order, and moved SYS-5 after it. This is the second time an approval went unrecorded (SABA-B-7 was the first). I also added lesson L47: an action that removes the focused element must name where focus goes; `lessons.md` is at 53 lines.

**SABA-B-7 preparation:** Ableton's Live 12 manual does not publish its volume fader curve. So round 234 has to define CZABA's own taper with a decision ID, and C will measure against that, not against a "Live formula". The two consult results are saved, and I filed `youtube-request.json` with five search queries for root. Next after round 233 is SABA-B-7, unless planning falls on or after 2026-10-30, when the regression round comes first.

The advisor was available and reviewed the plan twice; I applied its four corrections. Nothing in `store/` was changed: HEAD is `bd71144`, the working tree is clean, and the frozen hash list checks out. The planning files are all in `tmp/studio-real-loop`. The main ones:
- `current-task.md`
- `tasks/round-232.md`
- `b-round-232.md`
- `b-next.json`
